title: Find endpoint consumers by the route path as text, not only by type

mentor.identity: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) in the maintainer's evolution Step 12 session, following docs/chayen/MENTOR_BRIEF.md

existingGuidance.note: Step 6 says to find 'the frontend calls that hit a changed endpoint' but not how; the failing transcript searched for the Order interface only.
String occurrences name server-side route templates and serialization names, not client calls built from a URL string.
Verification asks for symbol-search and text-search counts but does not say what text to search for an endpoint.

rejectedCauses.why: The expected Skill loaded (Skill event for chayen-repository in the failing transcript).
Both consumers are in the repository; no .chayen/ map was involved, and the recipe's search steps apply without one.
Not shown: the recipe never names the route-string search, so the agent's type-only search is consistent with the guidance as written. A live run is needed before blaming the model.

diagnosis.rationale: The recipe tells the agent what to find but leaves the search method for endpoint consumers implicit. A consumer that builds the URL as a string and reads an untyped body is invisible to symbol search, which is exactly what FC-0002 records. Making the route-string search explicit in the existing step is the smallest change.

action.summary: In step 6 of the impact recipe, say how to find endpoint consumers: search every app for the route path as text, because untyped calls share no symbol with the server.

review.before: Asked to rename a response field, the agent searches for the typed Order interface, finds the Angular admin service, and declares it the only consumer; apps/shop/lib/order-status.ts is missed.
review.after: The agent searches for the route path text (api/orders) across apps, finds both the typed admin service and the untyped storefront helper, and lists both with path:line.
risks: Route text search can over-report (comments, docs, server route templates); the recipe already asks for path:line evidence per consumer, which filters these.
Routing collision: none. Only a reference body changes; no SKILL.md description or When to use section changes, so Skill selection is unaffected.
Token cost: three added lines in a reference that loads only for impact analysis.
